blindSummary: The national research examined this state/province and found no local trans statute or enforcement series of its own; it has not constituted the mandated transgender welfare board. National law applies uniformly here — there is no regional criminalisation — and no local divergence from the national framework was documented.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation's statement (26 March 2026) on the national parliament's 2026 amendment to the transgender-rights law: it removes self-identification, limits recognition to the country's traditional third-gender-community and intersex categories, mandates medical certification, and creates offences carrying up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' someone to be transgender. National law applies uniformly in this state/province; the piece records no local findings.

A national broadcaster's report (26 March 2026): both houses passed the amendment ending self-identification and mandating medical-board certification for recognition and gender-affirming surgery amid community and opposition protests; a supreme-court-appointed panel sought withdrawal, and presidential assent is pending. The law applies nationally, including in this state/province; the article has no local angle.

A national newspaper's city report (18 August 2024): a trans woman alleged a railway-security constable groped her during a 'gender check' at a metro station and made a lewd remark; authorities denied it and filed a counter-complaint. An incident from a different state/province, kept as a national datapoint on security screening of gender-nonconforming people in public spaces — a practice that would apply wherever comparable transport checkpoints exist.
